@graph.name: Flow Wrap Case Packer
@graph.description: A flow wrap case packer is a top-load machine that loads flow packs, the horizontally wrapped packages produced by flow wrappers, into shipping cases in a set count, pattern and orientation. TRF Industrial Automation packs flow packs with TRFRapidpack, the robotic case packer built for high-mix lines.

mainEntity.name: Is a Flow Pack the Same as a Flow Wrap?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Flow wrap, flow pack and horizontal form-fill-seal describe the same package: a tube of film formed around the product, sealed along its length and crimped at both ends. Buyers in the US usually say flow wrap or flow wrapped product, and TRF uses flow pack for the same soft, roughly rectangular package. On this page, all of these terms mean one package.

mainEntity.name: Can Several Flow Wrappers Feed One Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, when the combined rate and the layout allow it. TRF reviews how many wrappers feed the packer, how packages arrive, how much accumulation exists and how the flow behaves when one wrapper stops. The infeed, the picking method and the collation are then defined for the combined flow, often with vision guidance when lanes merge.

mainEntity.name: How Does a Case Packer Protect Delicate or Irregularly Shaped Products?

acceptedAnswer.text: By controlling the pick, the placement and the load in the case. The tool holds the package securely without pressing on the product and releases it in position rather than dropping it. TRFRapidpack is designed for controlled handling of delicate, flexible or irregularly shaped products, and TRF checks broken product, seal condition and pattern stability with real flow packs.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute, TRFOnepack for about 20 to 50 and TRFDroppack for about 20 to 500. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the flow pack, the pick tool, the pack pattern and the infeed, and TRF engineering validates it for each line.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. TRFIntraflow carries sealed cases to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, and interfaces with your wrappers and existing equipment are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: operators casing packages by hand per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, wrapper output lost to packing backlogs, broken product and time saved at flavor and format changes. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
